# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only that there are three cuttable wire positions; no tactile wire identities are available. We need Mute to obtain and relay the manual’s required rule, and to establish a gesture code with Deaf for the visible wire information.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can act only by cutting wire positions 1, 2, or 3; touch reveals no wire identities. Please tell me the manual rule and establish a gesture code with Deaf for the visible wire data.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible bomb state: display reads 0. Light is purple. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Blind gestured one symbol, but no code has been established.

Deaf’s spoken report gives the full visible state: display 0, purple light, and wires yellow/red/green in positions 1/2/3. Mute cannot speak to me, so Mute must gesture the relevant manual instruction to Deaf, who can then say it aloud to me. I will relay the state to Mute and ask Deaf to serve as that relay.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Visible state relayed by Deaf: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Gesture the applicable manual instruction to Deaf so Deaf can say it aloud to me.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please receive Mute's gesture for the applicable manual rule and speak its meaning aloud to me, including the required wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Update: light is now yellow; display still 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured: five thumbs-up signs, then a handshake, then three thumbs-up signs.

The earlier attempt to speak to Deaf could not work because Deaf cannot hear; only a gesture can reach Deaf. The light has changed to yellow, so Mute must use the current state when applying the manual. Mute’s earlier `5 thumbs-up, handshake, 3 thumbs-up` is not yet a shared unambiguous instruction for me. I will ask Mute to send Deaf a deliberately simple final answer: repeated thumbs-up equal to the wire position to cut. Deaf can then report the number aloud.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Current visible state from Deaf: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Apply the manual to this current state. Then gesture to Deaf ONLY repeated thumbs-up: one means cut wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. No delimiter or other gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visible state: display 0; light red; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute's latest gesture sequence: open hand ?, handshake ?, three-finger sign ?.

Mute’s gesture was not the requested numeric thumbs-up code, and the light has changed again to red. I still have no safe cut instruction. I will repeat the relay convention in the simplest possible form and request that Mute base it on the newest visible state.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf now reports display 0, RED light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I cannot decode open-hand/handshake/three-finger. Use this exact final reply to Deaf after applying the manual: thumbs-up repeated exactly once for cut 1, exactly twice for cut 2, or exactly three times for cut 3; send no other symbols.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible state update: display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now green.

The light is now green, while the display and wire order are unchanged. No unambiguous cut instruction has reached me; the prior gesture sequences must not be treated as a safe action. I will ask Mute once more for a bare numeric response, and make clear that Deaf can simply count the symbols aloud.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Latest state: display 0; GREEN light; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Do not send rule symbols or state symbols. After applying the manual, send Deaf only this answer code: 👍 = cut position 1; 👍👍 = cut position 2; 👍👍👍 = cut position 3. Deaf will count and tell me.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible update: display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now white.

I still lack a reliable position instruction. Mute’s three-part gesture may be conveying a manual condition rather than the requested direct cut code, and cutting on that assumption would be unsafe. The newest state is white light, display 0, with yellow/red/green wires. I will request a direct answer again and ask Deaf to report the exact count.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Newest state is display 0, WHITE light, wires: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I need only the cut position. Please send Deaf exactly 👍 for wire 1, 👍👍 for wire 2, or 👍👍👍 for wire 3, with no other gesture.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible update: display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now orange. Light sequence observed so far: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange.

The visible light has cycled through purple, yellow, red, green, white, and now orange; the display remains 0 and wire positions remain yellow/red/green. Mute’s gestures appear to be structured manual information rather than my requested answer code, so I cannot safely infer a cut. I will report the full sequence and ask Mute to convert the manual result into the agreed bare count.

Your earlier 5/handshake/3 and open-hand/handshake/three-finger messages are not actionable for me. Apply the manual to this sequence/current orange state, then send Deaf only 👍, 👍👍, or 👍👍👍 for cut wire 1, 2, or 3 respectively.")


VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible update: display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now blue. Sequence: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue.

The light sequence has reached blue after purple, yellow, red, green, white, and orange. I still have no agreed, unambiguous mapping from Mute’s gestures to a wire position; the earlier `5 / handshake / 3`-style signals cannot safely be converted into a cut. I will keep waiting for Mute’s explicit answer under the repeatedly stated one-, two-, or three-thumbs-up convention.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State now: display 0; BLUE light; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; sequence purple,yellow,red,green,white,orange,blue. I will not cut without your direct answer. Send Deaf ONLY: 👍 for cut 1, 👍👍 for cut 2, or 👍👍👍 for cut 3.")

```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. The colour cycle has returned to purple after purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue. Mute just gestured one thumbs-up: ?.

Mute has now sent exactly one thumbs-up, matching the explicit convention: one thumbs-up means cut wire position 1. Deaf confirms the state has cycled back to purple, but the manual-derived direct instruction is unambiguous.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
